info.name: IJS Vault - App APIs
info.description:
Complete API collection for IJS Vault mobile/web application.

## 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Set Environment**: Choose `Production` or `Development` environment
2. **Login**: Call the Login endpoint - tokens are automatically saved
3. **Use APIs**: All endpoints inherit the `{{accessToken}}` automatically

## 🔐 Authentication

All protected endpoints use `Bearer {{accessToken}}` which is automatically set after login.

## 📍 Environments

| Environment | Base URL |
|-------------|----------|
| Production | https://ijsvault.codecoytechnologies.live/v1 |
| Development | http://localhost:3000/v1 |

## 📁 API Sections

- **Authentication**: Register, Login, Social Auth, Password Reset
- **User Profile**: Profile management, Search users
- **Linked Users**: View shared files/folders per user with search, filter, sort
- **Vault**: Files, Folders, Sharing, PIN protection
- **File Uploads**: Direct, Presigned, Resumable uploads
- **Reminders**: Task reminders with email notifications
- **Notifications**: In-app notifications
- **Audit Logs**: Activity tracking

## 💡 Tips

- Tokens auto-refresh on login/register
- Use `{{itemId}}` variable for testing item operations
- Check folder descriptions for detailed API docs

item.name: Authentication

request.description:
**Register New User**

Create a new account with email and password.

**Automatic Actions:**
- Sends welcome email with 6-digit OTP code
- OTP valid for 10 minutes
- Returns access and refresh tokens

**Request Body:**
- `fullName` (required): User's full name, min 2 characters
- `email` (required): Valid email address
- `password` (required): Min 8 characters, must contain letter and number
- `phone` (optional): Phone number in E.164 format (e.g., +1234567890)
- `profilePic` (optional): URL to profile picture (upload via /users/profile-picture first)

**Response:**
- User object with subscription details
- Access token (expires in 30 minutes)
- Refresh token (expires in 30 days)

**Email Sent:**
Beautiful HTML email with:
- Welcome message
- Verification link button
- 6-digit OTP code in styled box
- Security tips

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "id": "user-id",
      "fullName": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "phone": "+1234567890",
      "image": "https://example.com/profile.jpg",
      "role": "user",
      "isEmailVerified": false,
      "subscription": {
        "plan": "free",
        "storageLimit": 16106127360,
        "storageUsed": 0
      }
    },
    "tokens": {
      "access": { "token": "...", "expires": "..." },
      "refresh": { "token": "...", "expires": "..." }
    }
  },
  "message": "Registration successful"
}
```

**Login with Email & Password**

Authenticate user and get access tokens.

**⚠️ One Device at a Time Policy:**
- When you login, ALL previous sessions are automatically terminated
- Only one active session per user is allowed
- Previous devices will receive 401 error on next API call

**Automatic Actions:**
- Terminates all existing sessions (one device policy)
- Creates new session with device info
- Sends login notification email (async)
- Includes IP address, device info, timestamp

**Request Body:**
- `email` (required): User's email address
- `password` (required): User's password
- `deviceType` (optional): ANDROID, IOS, WEB, HUAWEI, DESKTOP
- `deviceName` (optional): Device name for session tracking
- `deviceModel` (optional): Device model

**Response:**
- User object with all details
- Access token (30 min expiry)
- Refresh token (30 days expiry)

**Session Tracking:**
- Session created with device info
- lastActivityAt updated on each API call
- Session can be terminated by admin

**Error Responses:**
- 401: Incorrect email or password
- 400: Validation error

**Example Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "id": "user-id",
      "fullName": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "phone": "+1234567890",
      "role": "user",
      "isEmailVerified": true,
      "image": "http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/profile-123.jpg"
    },
    "tokens": {
      "access": { "token": "...", "expires": "..." },
      "refresh": { "token": "...", "expires": "..." }
    }
  },
  "message": "Login successful"
}
```

**Security:**
- Password verified with bcrypt
- Login activity tracked
- Email notification for security
- One device at a time enforced

**Logout User**

Invalidate refresh token and logout.

**Request Body:**
- `refreshToken` (required): The refresh token to invalidate

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { "loggedOut": true },
  "message": "Logged out successfully"
}
```

**What Happens:**
- Refresh token is removed from database
- Token becomes invalid immediately
- Access token remains valid until expiry
- User must login again to get new tokens

**Error Responses:**
- 404: Token not found (already logged out or invalid)

**Note:** Access tokens cannot be invalidated (JWT stateless). They expire after 30 minutes.

**Request Password Reset OTP**

Send password reset email with 6-digit OTP code.

**Request Body:**
- `email` (required): User's email address

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "message": "Password reset OTP sent successfully",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "otpExpiresIn": "10 minutes"
  },
  "message": "Password reset OTP sent"
}
```

**Email Sent:**
Beautiful HTML email with:
- 6-digit OTP code in styled box
- Security warnings
- Instructions

**OTP Details:**
- 6-digit numeric code
- Valid for 10 minutes only
- Single use (deleted after use)

**Security:**
- OTP expires after 10 minutes
- OTP deleted after successful reset
- Email includes security tips

**Next Step:** Use the Reset Password endpoint with the OTP to set a new password.

**Verify OTP (General Purpose)**

Verify any OTP code for different purposes: email verification, password reset confirmation, etc.

**Request Body:**
- `email` (required): User's email address
- `otp` (required): 6-digit OTP code from email (exactly 6 digits)
- `type` (optional): Type of verification - `emailVerification` (default), `resetPassword`, `passwordChange`

**Response for emailVerification:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { "verified": true },
  "message": "Email verified successfully"
}
```

**Response for other types:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { "verified": true, "type": "resetPassword" },
  "message": "OTP verified successfully"
}
```

**What Happens:**
- OTP is validated against database for the specified type
- For emailVerification: User's `isEmailVerified` set to true
- OTP is deleted after successful verification

**OTP Details:**
- 6-digit numeric code
- Valid for 10 minutes
- Single use only
- Type-specific (emailVerification OTP won't work for resetPassword)

**Error Responses:**
- 401: Invalid or expired OTP
- 404: User not found
- 400: Validation error (OTP must be 6 digits)

**Use Cases:**
- Email verification after registration
- Confirming password reset request
- Any OTP-based verification flow

**Reset Password with OTP**

Reset user password using OTP from email.

**Request Body:**
- `email` (required): User's email address
- `otp` (required): 6-digit OTP code from forgot password email
- `password` (required): New password (min 8 chars, letter + number)

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "passwordReset": true,
    "message": "Password has been reset successfully. You can now login with your new password."
  },
  "message": "Password reset successful"
}
```

**Automatic Actions:**
- OTP is verified and deleted
- Password is hashed with bcrypt
- Password change notification email sent
- User can login with new password immediately

**Email Sent:**
Password changed notification with:
- Confirmation message
- Timestamp of change
- Security warning if user didn't make change
- Instructions to secure account

**Error Responses:**
- 401: Invalid or expired OTP
- 404: User not found
- 400: Password validation failed

**Security:**
- OTP valid for 10 minutes only
- OTP deleted after use
- Email notification sent

**Flow:**
1. Call Forgot Password to receive OTP via email
2. Call this endpoint with email, OTP, and new password

**Resend Email Verification OTP**

Resend verification email with new OTP.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token in Authorization header

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "message": "Verification email sent successfully",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "otpExpiresIn": "10 minutes"
  },
  "message": "Verification email sent"
}
```

**Email Sent:**
Beautiful HTML email with:
- Welcome message with user's name
- 6-digit OTP code in styled box
- Security tips
- 10-minute expiration notice

**OTP Details:**
- 6-digit numeric code
- Valid for 10 minutes
- Stored in database
- Single use (deleted after verification)

**Use Cases:**
- User didn't receive first email
- OTP expired
- User lost verification email

**Next Step:** Use the Verify OTP endpoint with type `emailVerification` to verify the email.

**Send Password Change OTP**

Request an OTP to change your password. Requires verification of current password first.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token in Authorization header

**Request Body:**
- `currentPassword` (required): Your current password for verification

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "message": "Password change OTP sent successfully",
    "email": "john@example.com",
    "otpExpiresIn": "10 minutes"
  },
  "message": "Password change OTP sent"
}
```

**Email Sent:**
Beautiful HTML email with:
- Password change request notification
- 6-digit OTP code in styled box
- Security warning if user didn't request
- 10-minute expiration notice

**Security Flow:**
1. User must provide current password (prevents unauthorized changes)
2. If password is correct, OTP is generated and emailed
3. User uses OTP with Change Password endpoint

**Error Responses:**
- 401: Current password is incorrect
- 401: Please authenticate (invalid/missing token)

**Next Step:** Use the Change Password endpoint with the OTP received via email.

**Change Password with OTP**

Change your password using the OTP received from Send Password Change OTP endpoint.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token in Authorization header

**Request Body:**
- `otp` (required): 6-digit OTP code from password change email
- `newPassword` (required): New password (min 8 chars, must contain letter + number)

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "passwordChanged": true,
    "message": "Password has been changed successfully."
  },
  "message": "Password changed successfully"
}
```

**Automatic Actions:**
- OTP is verified and deleted
- Password is hashed with bcrypt
- Password change notification email sent
- User can login with new password immediately

**Email Sent:**
Password changed notification with:
- Confirmation message
- Timestamp of change
- Security warning if user didn't make change

**Error Responses:**
- 401: Invalid or expired OTP
- 401: Please authenticate (invalid/missing token)
- 400: Password validation failed (must be 8+ chars with letter and number)

**Complete Flow:**
1. Call Send Password Change OTP with current password
2. Receive OTP via email
3. Call this endpoint with OTP and new password

**Google Social Login**

Login or register using Google account via Firebase.

**Request Body:**
- `idToken` (required): Firebase Google ID token from client

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": { ... },
    "tokens": { ... },
    "isNewUser": false
  },
  "message": "Login successful"
}
```

**How It Works:**
1. Client authenticates with Google via Firebase
2. Client sends Firebase ID token to backend
3. Backend verifies token with Firebase
4. If user exists: Login
5. If new user: Auto-register

**Auto-Registration:**
- Email from Google account
- Name from Google profile
- Email pre-verified
- No password needed
- Social account linked

**Firebase Setup Required:**
- Firebase project configured
- Google sign-in enabled
- Firebase SDK in client app

**Security:**
- Token verified with Firebase
- Email verified by Google
- Secure OAuth flow

**Apple Social Login**

Login or register using Apple ID via Firebase.

**Request Body:**
- `idToken` (required): Firebase Apple ID token from client

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": { ... },
    "tokens": { ... },
    "isNewUser": false
  },
  "message": "Login successful"
}
```

**How It Works:**
1. Client authenticates with Apple via Firebase
2. Client sends Firebase ID token to backend
3. Backend verifies token with Firebase
4. If user exists: Login
5. If new user: Auto-register

**Auto-Registration:**
- Email from Apple ID (may be private)
- Name from Apple account
- Email pre-verified
- No password needed
- Social account linked

**Firebase Setup Required:**
- Firebase project configured
- Apple sign-in enabled
- Apple Developer account
- Service ID configured

**Security:**
- Token verified with Firebase
- Email verified by Apple
- Secure OAuth flow
- Privacy-focused

**Link Social Account**

Link a social account (Google/Apple) to an existing user account.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Request Body:**
- `idToken` (required): Firebase ID token from social login

**Note:** The provider (google/apple) is automatically detected from the Firebase token. Do NOT send provider in the request body.

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "socialAccount": {
      "userId": "user-id",
      "provider": "google",
      "providerId": "firebase-uid",
      "email": "user@gmail.com"
    }
  },
  "message": "Social account linked successfully"
}
```

**Error Responses:**
- 400: Cannot link password provider
- 409: Social account already linked
- 401: Invalid Firebase token

variable.description: Provider to unlink: google, apple, or facebook

request.description:
**Unlink Social Account**

Remove a linked social account from the user's profile.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Path Parameters:**
- `provider` (required): The provider to unlink - `google`, `apple`, or `facebook`

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {},
  "message": "Social account unlinked successfully"
}
```

**Error Responses:**
- 404: Social account not found
- 400: Cannot unlink - must have at least one login method (password or another social account)

**Note:** You cannot unlink your last login method. If you only have one social account linked and no password set, you must either set a password or link another social account before unlinking.

item.description:
Complete authentication system with OTP-based verification, social login, and security features.

**Features:**
- Email/Password registration and login
- Email verification with OTP (6-digit code)
- Password reset with OTP (6-digit code)
- Social login (Google, Apple) via Firebase
- JWT-based authentication
- Refresh token rotation
- Login notifications via email
- Password change notifications

**Security:**
- Passwords hashed with bcrypt
- JWT tokens with expiration
- OTP-based verification (no links)
- Login activity tracking
- Automatic security notifications

item.name: User Profile

request.description:
**Search Users for Linking**

Search for users by name or email to link/share vault items with.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Query Parameters:**
- `query` (required): Search term (min 2, max 100 characters)
  - Searches in: fullName, email
  - Case-insensitive
  - Partial match supported

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "users": [
      {
        "id": "user-id",
        "fullName": "John Doe",
        "email": "john@example.com",
        "image": "http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/profile-123.jpg"
      }
    ]
  },
  "message": "Users found"
}
```

**Features:**
- Excludes current user from results
- Returns users with matching name or email
- Limited to 20 results
- Returns only: id, fullName, email, image

**Use Cases:**
- Finding users to share vault items
- Adding collaborators
- Linking accounts

**Validation:**
- Query must be at least 2 characters
- Query cannot exceed 100 characters

**Error Responses:**
- 400: Query too short or invalid
- 401: Unauthorized (invalid token)

**Update User Profile**

Update current user's profile information.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Request Body (all optional, at least 1 required):**
```json
{
  "fullName": "John Doe",
  "phone": "+1234567890"
}
```

**Field Specifications:**

**fullName:**
- Type: String
- Min length: 2 characters
- Max length: 100 characters
- Example: "John Michael Doe"

**phone:**
- Type: String (E.164 format)
- Pattern: `^\+?[1-9]\d{1,14}$`
- Optional: Can be empty string or null to remove
- Examples:
  - `"+14155552671"` (US)
  - `"+442071838750"` (UK)
  - `"+919876543210"` (India)

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "id": "user-id",
      "fullName": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "phone": "+1234567890",
      "image": "http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/profile-123.jpg",
      "role": "user",
      "isEmailVerified": true,
      "notificationPreferences": { ... },
      "subscription": { ... }
    }
  },
  "message": "Profile updated successfully"
}
```

**Validation Errors (400):**
- `fullName` too short (< 2 chars)
- `fullName` too long (> 100 chars)
- `phone` invalid format
- No fields provided

**Example Payloads:**

**Update name only:**
```json
{
  "fullName": "Jane Smith"
}
```

**Update phone only:**
```json
{
  "phone": "+14155552671"
}
```

**Remove phone:**
```json
{
  "phone": ""
}
```

**Update both:**
```json
{
  "fullName": "John Doe",
  "phone": "+1234567890"
}
```

**Note:** Email cannot be changed via this endpoint for security reasons.

formdata.description: Optional: User ID to update profile picture for existing user

request.description:
**Upload Profile Picture (No Auth Required)**

Upload profile picture. Can be used during signup flow before user is created.

**No Authentication Required** - This endpoint is public to support signup flow.

Upload or update user's profile picture.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Request:**
- Method: POST
- Content-Type: multipart/form-data
- Body: Form field "image" with file

**File Specifications:**

**Allowed Formats:**
- JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg)
- PNG (.png)
- GIF (.gif)
- WebP (.webp)

**File Size:**
- Maximum: 5MB
- Recommended: < 2MB for optimal performance

**Image Dimensions:**
- Recommended: 400x400px (square)
- Minimum: 100x100px
- Aspect ratio: Any (will be displayed as circle)

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "user": {
      "id": "user-id",
      "fullName": "John Doe",
      "email": "john@example.com",
      "image": "http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/profile-1234567890.jpg",
      ...
    },
    "imageUrl": "http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/profile-1234567890.jpg"
  },
  "message": "Profile picture uploaded successfully"
}
```

**What Happens:**
1. Old profile picture is deleted (if exists)
2. New image is saved to `/uploads/profiles/`
3. Filename format: `profile-{userId}-{timestamp}.{ext}`
4. User's `image` field is updated with public URL
5. Image is accessible via HTTP

**Storage:**
- Location: Local file system
- Path: `/uploads/profiles/`
- Public URL: `http://localhost:3000/uploads/profiles/{filename}`

**Error Responses:**

**400 - No file provided:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "No image file provided"
}
```

**400 - Invalid file type:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "Only image files are allowed"
}
```

**413 - File too large:**
```json
{
  "code": 413,
  "message": "File too large. Maximum size is 5MB"
}
```

**cURL Example:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:3000/v1/users/profile-picture \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_TOKEN" \
  -F "image=@/path/to/photo.jpg"
```

**Postman:**
1. Select POST method
2. Add Authorization header with Bearer token
3. Go to Body tab
4. Select "form-data"
5. Add key "image" with type "File"
6. Choose your image file
7. Send request

**Best Practices:**
- Use square images for best display
- Compress images before upload
- Use JPEG for photos, PNG for graphics
- Keep file size under 2MB

**Update Notification Preferences**

Configure which notifications user wants to receive.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Request Body (all optional, at least 1 required):**
```json
{
  "reminders": true,
  "linkedUsersActivity": true,
  "inviteNotifications": false
}
```

**Notification Types:**

**reminders** (boolean)
- Receive reminder notifications
- Triggers: When vault item reminder is due
- Channels: Email, Push (if enabled)
- Default: `true`

**linkedUsersActivity** (boolean)
- Notifications for linked users' activity
- Triggers: When linked user shares/updates items
- Channels: Email, Push
- Default: `true`

**inviteNotifications** (boolean)
- Receive invite notifications
- Triggers: When invited to share vault items
- Channels: Email, Push
- Default: `true`

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "preferences": {
      "reminders": true,
      "linkedUsersActivity": true,
      "inviteNotifications": false
    }
  },
  "message": "Notification preferences updated"
}
```

**Example Payloads:**

**Disable all notifications:**
```json
{
  "reminders": false,
  "linkedUsersActivity": false,
  "inviteNotifications": false
}
```

**Enable only reminders:**
```json
{
  "reminders": true,
  "linkedUsersActivity": false,
  "inviteNotifications": false
}
```

**Update single preference:**
```json
{
  "reminders": false
}
```

**Enable all:**
```json
{
  "reminders": true,
  "linkedUsersActivity": true,
  "inviteNotifications": true
}
```

**Validation:**
- All fields must be boolean
- At least one field required
- Invalid field names are ignored

**Error Responses:**

**400 - No fields provided:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "At least one preference must be provided"
}
```

**400 - Invalid type:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "reminders must be a boolean"
}
```

**Use Cases:**
- User wants to reduce notification noise
- Disable notifications during vacation
- Enable only critical notifications
- Customize notification experience

**Note:** These preferences affect both email and push notifications.

item.description:
User profile management endpoints for authenticated users.

**Features:**
- Update profile information (name, phone)
- Upload and manage profile picture
- Configure notification preferences
- Search for users to link/share with
- View linked users

**Authentication:**
All endpoints require Bearer token authentication.

**Profile Fields:**
- `fullName`: User's full name (2-100 characters)
- `phone`: Phone number in E.164 format (e.g., +1234567890)
- `image`: Profile picture URL (auto-generated on upload)

**Notification Preferences:**
- `reminders`: Receive reminder notifications (boolean)
- `linkedUsersActivity`: Notifications for linked users' activity (boolean)
- `inviteNotifications`: Receive invite notifications (boolean)

item.name: Linked Users

request.description:
**Get Linked Users (Basic List)**

Retrieve a simple list of users linked to your account.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "users": [
      {
        "id": "user-id",
        "fullName": "Jane Smith",
        "email": "jane@example.com",
        "image": "https://example.com/profile.jpg"
      }
    ]
  },
  "message": "Linked users retrieved"
}
```

**What are Linked Users?**
- Users you've shared vault items with
- Users who have shared items with you
- Collaborators on shared folders

**Response Fields:**
- `id`: User's unique identifier
- `fullName`: User's full name
- `email`: User's email address
- `image`: Profile picture URL (if set)

**Use Cases:**
- Quick list of collaborators
- Populate user picker for sharing
- Display linked users count

**Note:** For detailed shared items per user, use `/users/linked/details` instead.

query.description: Search by user name or email (optional)
Filter by role: view, edit, or all (optional)
Sort by: name, recent, or mostShared (default: recent)

request.description:
**Get Linked Users with Detailed Shared Items**

Retrieve comprehensive list of linked users with all shared folders and files per user.

**Authentication:**
- Requires: Bearer token

**Query Parameters:**
- `search` (optional): Filter by user name or email
- `role` (optional): Filter by role - `view`, `edit`, or `all`
- `sortBy` (optional): Sort results - `name`, `recent`, or `mostShared` (default: recent)

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "users": [
      {
        "userId": "user-123",
        "fullName": "Jane Smith",
        "email": "jane@example.com",
        "image": "https://example.com/profile.jpg",
        "primaryRole": "edit",
        "roles": ["view", "edit"],
        "totalSharedCount": 5,
        "lastSharedAt": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z",
        "sharedItems": {
          "folders": [
            {
              "id": "folder-1",
              "name": "Work Documents",
              "role": "edit",
              "color": null,
              "parentId": null,
              "parentName": null,
              "sharedAt": "2026-01-15T10:00:00Z"
            }
          ],
          "files": [
            {
              "id": "file-1",
              "name": "Report.pdf",
              "role": "view",
```

request.description:
Get all items (folders and files) in a specific folder or root with advanced filtering, sorting, and pagination.

**Query Parameters:**

**Pagination:**
- `page`: Page number (default: 1, min: 1)
- `limit`: Items per page (default: 20, min: 1, max: 100)

**Filtering:**
- `parentId`: Parent folder ID (empty/null for root items)
- `type`: Filter by item type - `folder` or `file`
- `fileType`: Filter files by type - `document`, `media`, or `note` (automatically sets type=file)

**Sorting:**
- `sortBy`: Sort field - `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or `size`
- `sortOrder`: Sort direction - `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending)
- Default: Folders first, then by name ascending

**Example Queries:**
```
# Get folders only
?type=folder

# Get documents only
?fileType=document

# Sort by newest first
?sortBy=createdAt&sortOrder=desc

# Paginate with 10 items per page
?page=2&limit=10

# Combined: Get files sorted by name, page 1
?type=file&sortBy=name&sortOrder=asc&limit=20
```

**Response Structure:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "items": [...],
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "limit": 20,
      "totalCount": 45,
      "totalPages": 3,
      "hasNextPage": true,
      "hasPrevPage": false,
      "nextPage": 2,
      "prevPage": null
    }
  },
  "message": "Items retrieved successfully"
}
```

**Each item includes:**
- Basic info: `id`, `name`, `type`, `description`, `isLocked`
- Ownership: `ownerId` (populated with user details)
- Sharing: `linkedUsers` array with roles
- Timestamps: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`
- Navigation: `breadcrumb` object with full path
- Files only: `fileType`, `size`, `mimeType`, `extension`

**Important Notes:**
- File URLs are NOT exposed in listings for security
- Use `/vault/items/:id/download` endpoint to get secure download URLs
- Default sorting: Folders appear before files, then sorted by name
- When `sortBy` is specified, custom sorting overrides the default

Create a new folder. Only requires name. parentId is optional (null for root). Description is optional.

**Response includes breadcrumb** showing the folder's location in the hierarchy.
Get details of a specific item (folder or file) by ID. Returns full item details including owner, linked users, metadata, and **breadcrumb path**.

**Update Item**

Update item properties. Only owner or users with EDIT role can update basic fields.

**Updatable Fields:**
- `name`: New name (1-255 chars)
- `description`: New description
- `pin`: Set 4-digit PIN (owner only) or `null` to remove PIN
- `linkedUsers`: Array of users with individual roles (owner only)

**PIN Protection:**
- Set `pin` to 4-digit string to enable PIN protection
- Set `pin` to `null` to remove PIN protection
- Only owner can modify PIN

**Linked Users with Individual Roles:**
```json
{
  "linkedUsers": [
    {"userId": "user-id-1", "role": "view"},
    {"userId": "user-id-2", "role": "edit"}
  ]
}
```

**Response includes updated breadcrumb** if name changed.
Delete an item. Only owner can delete. Deleting a folder recursively deletes all children and their files from storage.
Move item to a different folder. Only owner can move items. Cannot move folder into itself or its descendants. Use null for root.
Copy item to a different folder. Only owner can copy items. Creates a duplicate with '(Copy)' appended to the name. Cannot copy folder into itself or its descendants. Use null for root.
Get breadcrumb path from root to this item. Returns array of parent folders for navigation.
Check user's access level to an item. Returns hasAccess, role (owner/view/edit), and isLocked status.
Search items by name or description. Supports filtering by type and fileType. Returns items user owns or has access to.
Get presigned URL for large file upload (> 100MB). See 'File Uploads' folder for all upload methods including resumable uploads.
Delete multiple items at once. Only owner can delete items. Folders are recursively deleted.
Move multiple items to a new folder at once. Only owner can move items. Use null for root.
Get all items shared with current user. Returns items where user is in linkedUsers array.
Get items inside a shared folder. User must have access to the parent folder.
Set 4-digit PIN on item. Only owner can set PIN. PIN is hashed with bcrypt before storage.

**Verify PIN to Access Locked Item**

Verify PIN to access a locked item. Both owner and shared users must verify PIN.

**Security: 3-Attempt Lockout**
- User has 3 attempts to enter correct PIN
- After 3 failed attempts, user is locked out
- Locked out user must log in again to reset attempts
- Security email is sent on lockout

**Success Response (200):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "verified": true,
    "sessionExpiresIn": 900
  },
  "message": "PIN verified successfully..."
}
```

**Wrong PIN - Attempts Remaining (401):**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Unauthorized",
  "message": "Invalid PIN. 2 attempts remaining.",
  "data": {
    "lockedOut": false,
    "remainingAttempts": 2
  }
}
```

**Lockout - 3rd Failed Attempt (403):**
```json
{
  "success": false,
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "message": "Too many failed PIN attempts. You have been logged out for security. Please log in again.",
  "data": {
    "lockedOut": true,
    "requiresRelogin": true,
    "remainingAttempts": 0
  }
}
```

**Frontend Action on Lockout:**
1. Clear local tokens (access + refresh)
2. Show security message to user
3. Redirect to login screen
Remove PIN from item. Only owner can remove PIN.

**Lock Item (Revoke PIN Session)**

Manually lock an item before the 15-minute unlock session expires.

**Use Case:**
- User wants to immediately lock an item after viewing
- User is leaving their device and wants to secure items

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "locked": true,
    "itemId": "item-id"
  },
  "message": "Item locked successfully. PIN verification required for next access."
}
```

**Note:** This only revokes the PIN session. The item still has PIN protection enabled.

**Get PIN Session Status**

Check if item is currently unlocked and how much time remains.

**Use for:**
- Displaying unlock timer on frontend
- Checking if PIN verification is needed before download

**Response (Item Unlocked):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "isLocked": true,
    "hasPinProtection": true,
    "sessionActive": true,
    "remainingSeconds": 720
  },
  "message": "Item unlocked for 720 more seconds"
}
```

**Response (Item Locked):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "isLocked": true,
    "hasPinProtection": true,
    "sessionActive": false,
    "remainingSeconds": 0
  },
  "message": "Item is locked. PIN verification required."
}
```

**Response (No PIN Protection):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "isLocked": false,
    "hasPinProtection": false,
    "sessionActive": false,
    "remainingSeconds": 0
  },
  "message": "Item is not PIN protected"
}
```

**Share Item with Users**

Share item with other users. Only owner can share.

**Two Formats Supported:**

**Option 1 - Individual Roles (Recommended):**
```json
{
  "users": [
    {"userId": "user-id-1", "role": "view"},
    {"userId": "user-id-2", "role": "edit"}
  ]
}
```

**Option 2 - Same Role for All (Backward Compatible):**
```json
{
  "userIds": ["user-id-1", "user-id-2"],
  "role": "view"
}
```

**Roles:**
- `view`: Read-only access
- `edit`: Can modify but not delete/share

**Actions:**
- Sends notification to shared users
- If user already shared, updates their role
Remove user's access to item. Only owner can unshare.
Secure file download. Checks access permissions and PIN verification before returning short-lived download URL (5 min expiry). For locked items, PIN must be verified first via /verify-pin endpoint.

item.description:
Secure file and folder management system (Google Drive-like).

**Features:**
- Create folders and files with unlimited nesting
- Protect items with 4-digit PIN codes (hashed with bcrypt)
- Share items with other users (VIEW or EDIT roles)
- Sort and filter items
- Move items between folders
- Search functionality
- **Breadcrumb navigation** - All item responses include breadcrumb path

**Breadcrumb Response:**
All item responses now include a `breadcrumb` object:
```json
{
  "breadcrumb": {
    "path": [
      { "id": null, "name": "Root" },
      { "id": "folder-id-1", "name": "Documents" },
      { "id": "folder-id-2", "name": "Work" }
    ],
    "pathString": "Root / Documents / Work"
  }
}
```

**Secure File Access:**
- File URLs are NOT exposed in item listings
- Use `/vault/items/:id/download` to get a short-lived (5 min) download URL
- PIN-protected files require PIN verification first

**Sharing Roles:**
- `view`: Can view and download items, verify PIN, but cannot edit or delete
- `edit`: Can view, edit, create files in shared folders, but cannot delete or share (owner only)

**PIN Protection:**
- 4-digit numeric PIN
- Hashed with bcrypt before storage
- Required for accessing locked items
- Shared users must also verify PIN

**Important Notes:**
- Folders no longer require `icon`, `color`, or `type` fields (simplified)
- Only owners can delete or share items
- Users with EDIT role can modify but not delete
- Deleting a folder recursively deletes all children

item.name: File Uploads

formdata.description: Parent folder ID (optional, null for root)

request.description:
**Direct File Upload (Small Files < 100MB)**

Simplest upload method. File is uploaded directly through the server.

**Use for:** Files under 100MB

**Request:**
- Content-Type: multipart/form-data
- file: The file to upload

formdata.description: Item ID to update image for (optional - leave empty for new items)

request.description:
**Upload Item Image (Custom Folder/File Icons)**

Upload custom images for folders and files to personalize your vault items.

**Use Cases:**
- Set custom folder icons (e.g., project logos, category images)
- Add preview images for files
- Personalize vault organization with visual identifiers

**Two Usage Modes:**

**Mode 1 - Update Existing Item:**
```
POST /vault/items/upload-image
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

image: <image file>
itemId: "existing-item-id"
```

**Mode 2 - Get URL for New Item:**
```
POST /vault/items/upload-image
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

image: <image file>
(no itemId - returns URL to use when creating item)
```

**File Specifications:**

**Allowed Formats:**
- JPEG (.jpg, .jpeg)
- PNG (.png)
- GIF (.gif)
- WebP (.webp)

**File Size:**
- Maximum: 5MB
- Recommended: < 1MB for optimal performance

**Image Dimensions:**
- Recommended: 512x512px (square)
- Minimum: 100x100px
- Any aspect ratio supported

**Success Response (with itemId):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "item": {
      "id": "item-id",
      "name": "My Folder",
      "type": "folder",
      "itemImage": "https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/item-userId-itemId-1234567890.jpg",
      "breadcrumb": [...],
      ...
    },
    "imageUrl": "https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/item-userId-itemId-1234567890.jpg"
  },
  "message": "Item image uploaded successfully"
}
```

**Success Response (without itemId):**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "imageUrl": "https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/item-userId-new-1234567890.jpg"
  },
  "message": "Item image uploaded successfully"
}
```

**What Happens:**
1. Image is validated (type, size)
2. Old image is deleted if updating existing item
3. New image is saved to `/uploads/items/`
4. Filename format: `item-{userId}-{itemId}-{timestamp}.{ext}`
5. Public HTTPS URL is generated with domain name
6. If itemId provided: Item's `itemImage` field is updated
7. Image is accessible via HTTPS

**Storage:**
- Location: VPS file system
- Path: `/uploads/items/`
- Public URL: `https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/{filename}`
- **Note:** URLs use domain name (not IP address) with HTTPS

**Error Responses:**

**400 - No file provided:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "No image file provided"
}
```

**400 - Invalid file type:**
```json
{
  "code": 400,
  "message": "Only image files are allowed (jpeg, jpg, png, gif, webp)"
}
```

**413 - File too large:**
```json
{
  "code": 413,
  "message": "File too large. Maximum size is 5MB"
}
```

**404 - Item not found:**
```json
{
  "code": 404,
  "message": "Item not found"
}
```

**403 - No access:**
```json
{
  "code": 403,
  "message": "You do not have access to this item"
}
```

**Complete Workflow Examples:**

**Example 1 - Update Existing Folder:**
```bash
# Upload image for existing folder
curl -X POST https://yourdomain.com/v1/vault/items/upload-image \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}" \
  -F "image=@folder-icon.png" \
  -F "itemId=6956daf969aedf2bd90667d3"

# Response includes updated item with itemImage field
```

**Example 2 - Create New Folder with Custom Image:**
```bash
# Step 1: Upload image first
curl -X POST https://yourdomain.com/v1/vault/items/upload-image \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}" \
  -F "image=@project-logo.png"

# Response: { "imageUrl": "https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/..." }

# Step 2: Create folder with the image URL
curl -X POST https://yourdomain.com/v1/vault/folders \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer {token}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Project Alpha",
    "itemImage": "https://yourdomain.com/uploads/items/...",
    "parentId": null
  }'
```

**Mobile/Web App Integration:**

**Display Logic:**
- If `itemImage` exists: Show custom image
- If `itemImage` is null/empty: Show default icon based on type
  - Folders: Default folder icon
  - Files: Icon based on file type (pdf, doc, image, etc.)

**UI Features:**
- Image picker for folders/files
- Preview before upload
- Crop/resize options (optional)
- Remove image button (set itemImage to null via update endpoint)

**Performance Tips:**
- Cache images on client side
- Use lazy loading for image grids
- Compress images before upload
- Consider thumbnail generation for large images

**Security:**
- Only authenticated users can upload
- User must have access to item to update its image
- File type validation prevents malicious uploads
- Size limit prevents abuse
- Old images automatically cleaned up

**Get Presigned Upload URL (Medium Files)**

Step 1 of 2-step upload for files up to 5GB.

**Flow:**
1. Call this endpoint to get presigned URL
2. Upload file directly to the URL using PUT
3. Call /confirm-upload to create the item

**Response:**
```json
{
  "uploadUrl": "https://...",
  "key": "vault/userId/timestamp-filename",
  "expiresIn": 3600
}
```

**Confirm Presigned Upload**

Step 2 of 2-step upload. Call after uploading to presigned URL.

Creates the item record in database.

**Initiate Resumable Upload (Large Files >100MB)**

Starts a multipart upload session. Use for files larger than 100MB.

**Request Body:**
- filename: Original filename
- contentType: MIME type
- size: File size in bytes (required for calculating parts)
- parentId: Optional folder ID
- description: Optional description

**Response:**
```json
{
  "uploadId": "abc123",
  "key": "vault/userId/timestamp-filename",
  "partSize": 5242880,
  "totalParts": 1024,
  "filename": "large-video.mp4"
}
```

**Next Step:** Use uploadId to get part URLs

**Get Presigned URLs for Parts**

Request up to 100 part URLs at once for parallel uploads.

**Request:**
- uploadId: From initiate response
- key: From initiate response
- partNumbers: Array of part numbers to get URLs for

**Response:**
```json
{
  "parts": [
    { "partNumber": 1, "uploadUrl": "https://...", "expiresIn": 3600 },
    { "partNumber": 2, "uploadUrl": "https://...", "expiresIn": 3600 }
  ]
}
```

**Upload each part:**
```
PUT {uploadUrl}
Body: <file chunk bytes>
```

**IMPORTANT:** Save the ETag from each response header!

**Check Upload Progress (for Resuming)**

Returns list of already uploaded parts.

**Use this to:**
- Resume an interrupted upload
- Track upload progress
- Identify missing parts

**Response:**
```json
{
  "uploadedParts": [
    { "partNumber": 1, "etag": "\"abc123\"", "size": 5242880 },
    { "partNumber": 2, "etag": "\"def456\"", "size": 5242880 }
  ],
  "uploadedPartsCount": 2,
  "totalUploadedBytes": 10485760
}
```

**To resume:** Only upload parts not in this list

**Complete Resumable Upload**

Call after ALL parts are uploaded successfully.

**Request:**
- uploadId, key: From initiate response
- parts: Array of {partNumber, etag} for each part
- filename, contentType, size: Original file info
- parentId, description: Optional

**IMPORTANT:** The etag must include quotes!

**Response:**
- Created item with breadcrumb
- File is now available in vault

**Abort/Cancel Resumable Upload**

Cleans up incomplete upload from storage.

**Use when:**
- User cancels upload
- Upload is no longer needed
- Want to start fresh

**Note:** Incomplete uploads are automatically cleaned up after 7 days

item.description:
File upload APIs for the Vault system.

**Three Upload Methods:**

| Method | Use Case | Max Size | Resumable |
|--------|----------|----------|----------|
| Direct Upload | Small files | ~100MB | No |
| Presigned URL | Medium files | ~5GB | No |
| **Resumable Upload** | **Large files** | **Unlimited** | **Yes** |

**Recommended Usage:**
- Files < 100MB: Use Direct Upload
- Files 100MB - 1GB: Use Presigned URL
- Files > 1GB: Use Resumable Upload

**Resumable Upload Flow (like Google Drive):**
1. `POST /resumable/initiate` - Start upload session
2. `POST /resumable/part-urls` - Get URLs for chunks
3. Upload chunks directly to presigned URLs
4. If error: `GET /resumable/progress` to check what uploaded
5. Resume by uploading only missing parts
6. `POST /resumable/complete` - Finalize upload

**Benefits of Resumable Upload:**
- Resume interrupted uploads
- Parallel chunk uploads for speed
- No data loss on network errors
- Progress tracking built-in

item.name: Reminders

query.description: Filter by status: pending, completed, overdue, snoozed

request.description:
**Get All Reminders**

Retrieve all reminders for the authenticated user with pagination.

**Query Parameters:**
- `status` (optional): Filter by status (pending, completed, overdue, snoozed)
- `itemId` (optional): Filter by vault item ID
- `page` (optional): Page number (default: 1)
- `limit` (optional): Items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

**Response:**
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "reminders": [...],
    "pagination": {
      "page": 1,
      "limit": 20,
      "totalCount": 45,
      "totalPages": 3,
      "hasNextPage": true,
      "hasPrevPage": false,
      "nextPage": 2,
      "prevPage": null
    }
  },
  "message": "Reminders retrieved successfully"
}
```

**Create Reminder**

Create a new reminder linked to a vault item.

**Request Body:**
- `title` (required): Reminder title (1-255 chars)
- `description` (optional): Detailed description
- `date` (required): Due date in YYYY-MM-DD format
- `time` (required): Due time in HH:MM 24-hour format
- `itemId` (required): ID of the vault item (file/folder)

**Example:**
```json
{
  "title": "Review Document",
  "description": "Check the quarterly report",
  "date": "2026-01-15",
  "time": "14:30",
  "itemId": "6956daf969aedf2bd90667d3"
}
```

**Note:** User must have access to the item to create a reminder for it.

**Get Reminder Statistics**

Get count of reminders by status.

**Response:**
```json
{
  "total": 10,
  "pending": 5,
  "completed": 3,
  "overdue": 1,
  "snoozed": 1
}
```

**Get Reminder by ID**

Retrieve a specific reminder by its ID.

**Update Reminder**

Update reminder details. At least one field required.

**Updatable Fields:**
- `title`: New title (1-255 chars)
- `description`: New description
- `date`: New date (YYYY-MM-DD)
- `time`: New time (HH:MM)

**Note:** Cannot change itemId or userId.

**Delete Reminder**

Permanently delete a reminder. Only the reminder owner can delete.

**Get Reminders for Item**

Get all reminders associated with a specific vault item.

**Update Reminder Status**

Change the status of a reminder.

**Valid Statuses:**
- `pending`: Mark as active/waiting
- `completed`: Mark as done (sets completedAt timestamp)
- `overdue`: Mark as past due
- `snoozed`: Mark as snoozed (use snooze endpoint instead)

**Snooze Reminder**

Postpone a reminder until a specified time.

**Request Body:**
- `snoozedUntil` (required): ISO 8601 datetime when reminder should reactivate

**What happens:**
- Status changes to 'snoozed'
- When snoozedUntil time passes, status returns to 'pending'
- Checked by the check-overdue endpoint

**Check Overdue Reminders**

Manually trigger check for overdue reminders. Typically called by a cron job.

**Actions performed:**
1. Find all pending reminders past their due time
2. Update status to 'overdue'
3. Send email notifications (if enabled)
4. Send push notifications (if FCM registered)
5. Create in-app notifications
6. Unsnooze reminders past their snooze time

**Response:**
```json
{
  "overdueCount": 3,
  "notifiedCount": 2,
  "unsnoozedCount": 1
}
```

item.description:
Reminder management for vault items.

**Features:**
- Create reminders linked to vault items (files/folders)
- Automatic status tracking (pending, completed, overdue, snoozed)
- Email notifications when reminders become due
- Push notifications via FCM
- Snooze functionality

**Reminder Statuses:**
- `pending`: Active reminder waiting for due time
- `overdue`: Past due time, notification sent
- `completed`: Marked as done by user
- `snoozed`: Temporarily postponed

**Automatic Actions:**
- When a reminder becomes overdue:

  - Email notification sent (if enabled)
  - Push notification sent (if FCM registered)
  - In-app notification created

**Date/Time Format:**
- date: `YYYY-MM-DD` (e.g., '2026-01-15')
- time: `HH:MM` 24-hour format (e.g., '14:30')

item.description:
In-app notification management with FCM-compatible format.

**Notification Types:**
- `share`: Someone shared an item with you (high priority, email sent)
- `edit`: Shared item was edited (normal priority)
- `delete`: Shared item was deleted (high priority, email sent)
- `move`: Shared item was moved (low priority)
- `unshare`: Your access was removed (high priority, email sent)
- `reminder`: Reminder is due/overdue (high priority, email sent)
- `system`: System announcements
- `admin_notification`: Admin broadcasts

**Features:**
- Automatic creation when events occur
- FCM push notifications sent automatically
- SMTP email notifications for important events
- Read/unread status tracking
- Bulk mark as read
- Linked to vault items when applicable
- Timestamps (sentAt, createdAt, updatedAt)

**Notification Channels:**
- `push`: FCM push notification
- `email`: SMTP email notification
- `inApp`: In-app notification (always enabled)

**Response Format (FCM-compatible):**
All notification responses include:
- `id`: Notification ID
- `type`: Notification type
- `title`: Notification title
- `body`: Notification body (same as message)
- `message`: Notification message
- `timestamp`: When notification was sent (ISO 8601)
- `priority`: low, normal, high, critical
- `icon`: Icon identifier
- `data`: Additional payload data
- `fcmSent`: Whether FCM push was sent
- `emailSent`: Whether email was sent

item.description:
Activity audit trail for vault items.

**Tracked Actions:**
- `create`: Item created (folder/file)
- `edit`: Item updated (name, description)
- `delete`: Item deleted
- `share`: Item shared with user
- `unshare`: User access removed
- `move`: Item moved to different folder
- `upload`: File uploaded
- `download`: File downloaded
- `pin_change`: PIN set/removed
- `reminder_set`: Reminder created for item

**Audit Log Entry Contains:**
- Who performed the action
- What action was performed
- Which item was affected
- When it happened
- Additional details (changes made, target user, etc.)

**Use Cases:**
- Security monitoring
- Activity tracking
- Compliance reporting
- Troubleshooting
